passages.t: ‘Vindicate me, O LORD!’, and ‘I love the house where You dwell’
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “Of David” (verse 1). He begins with a strong request: “Vindicate me, O LORD! For I have walked with integrity; I have trusted in the LORD without wavering” (verse 1). He invites God to look closely: “Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind” (verse 2).

He has kept away from people who cheat and plot. “I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites” (verse 4). “I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD” (verse 6).

At the centre is love for God's house. “O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides” (verse 8). He asks not to be swept away with the violent, “whose right hands are full of bribes” (verse 10).

Then: “But I will walk with integrity; redeem me and be merciful to me” (verse 11). It ends on solid ground: “My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the LORD” (verse 12).
passages.hearers:
This is the prayer of someone falsely accused, like Psalm 17. Israel's law sent cases too hard for the local judges to the priests at God's sanctuary (Deuteronomy 17:8-9). A person who could not prove his innocence before men could bring his case before God.

‘I wash my hands in innocence’ was a known sign. When a murder could not be solved, the elders of the nearest town washed their hands and said, “Our hands did not shed this blood” (Deuteronomy 21:7). Priests also washed their hands before going to the altar (Exodus 30:19). So the man is saying two things: I am clear of this charge, and I am ready to come near to God.

‘Heart and mind’ in verse 2 is in Hebrew ‘kidneys and heart’: the hidden motives and the thinking self. He asks God to search all of it.
passages.later:
In the trial of Jesus, Pilate also washed his hands and said, “I am innocent of this man's blood” (Matthew 27:24). But Pilate washed his hands while handing an innocent man over to death. The sign meant nothing without a clean heart.

David's other prayer goes deeper: “wash me, and I will be whiter than snow” (Psalm 51:7). John writes, “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins” (1 John 1:9).
passages.hard: ‘I have walked with integrity’ can sound proud. It is a claim to be innocent of a charge, not to be without sin, and verse 11 asks for mercy in the same breath. The book page explains this in ‘When a psalmist says he is innocent’.
passages.asks:
If you have been accused of something you did not do, the psalm lets you say so to God, plainly, and leave the verdict with him.

It also asks about your company (verses 4 and 5) and your love for worship (verse 8). Do you love the place where God's people gather, or only put up with it?
